headline: No ISO clears the T1->T2 rubric gate at HEAD — all six read HOLD — and no ISO clears the §2.1b full-solve authorization gate. THIS REFRESH MOVED NO DETERMINATION, NO VERDICT AND NO GATE OUTCOME. It re-derives the board's rows and prose from the LIVE committed verdict records in frontend/data/forecast/ff-verdicts.json (the un-suffixed per-tier keys, session FFR-3A-2, scored_at_sha 8ba59281), which most rows had drifted behind: they still quoted the preserved SUPERSEDED '-ff2d' vintage. THE HEADLINE CORRECTION IS CROSS-ISO. The I4/A1 capacity-accounting leak this board named as the dominant T1-F blocker is CLOSED — it appears in no live FC-1 fail set in any ISO, closed by the FFR-1A confirmed-derate recorder on 2026-07-31 — and closing it cleared FC-1 nowhere, because ADEQUACY ACCOUNTING was underneath it: I7 in CAISO/PJM/MISO/NYISO/NEISO and I12 in ERCOT/CAISO, 6 of 6 ISOs. PJM and NEISO are closest (one small I7 miss each: 366 MW and 218 MW); NYISO is on the cusp at 36/51 MW. Two corrections run AGAINST the board's favour and are reported at full magnitude (rule 1): ERCOT's I3 slack is 0.08-0.41% of load, not 0.01-0.03%, and its T1-X 2025 price no longer converges (22.5% FAIL, not 8.6% PASS). This board is the §2.1b evidence, not a green-wash: every remaining blocker is structural (rule 1).
gate_reading: The dominant T1-F blocker is FC-1 ADEQUACY ACCOUNTING — not the I4 leak, which is CLOSED (see honest_unfit 'I4 / A1'). I7 (accredited firm capacity below the reliability requirement) FAILs in CAISO, PJM, MISO, NYISO and NEISO; I12 (reserve-margin band) FAILs in ERCOT and CAISO. Together that is 6 of 6 ISOs, and in PJM, NEISO and NYISO it is the ONLY FC-1 failure left. PJM and NEISO are closest — a single small I7 miss each (PJM 2030, 366 MW = 0.24% of requirement; NEISO 2028, 218 MW = 0.85%). NYISO is on the cusp: 36 MW (2026) and 51 MW (2027), under 0.16% of requirement in both years. MISO is the same shape one order larger (6,037 / 3,659 MW). ERCOT and CAISO are furthest and differ in kind: both carry I12 band failures plus I3 scarcity slack, and CAISO additionally fails I7 in four consecutive years (to 9.2 GW) with a 65.5% backstop share — an administrative over-build, not a fleet the screen chose. The FF-2C capacity-clearing flip is the structurally-correct mechanism and is working; the residuals it exposes are the open adequacy-accounting / retirement-rule / backstop lanes, not tuning targets. WHAT THIS READING IS NOT: it is not a re-score. Every verdict quoted here already existed in a committed record; this refresh only stopped the board from describing a superseded one.
readiness: The FF-3E full-horizon readiness battery is GREEN for all six ISOs — the path is bug-free (input-resolution walk, config round-trip, kill-resume drill all clean; wall/RSS projected). Ten hours of compute today would buy a mechanically-clean but structurally-flawed golden run. Compute is not the binding constraint; the T1-F structural blockers are.

honest_unfit.title: Adequacy accounting — THE dominant T1-F blocker (6/6 ISOs)
honest_unfit.detail: PROMOTED 2026-08-24 to the dominant-blocker row, replacing I4/A1. Adequacy accounting is the ONLY FC-1 family still failing, and it reaches every ISO: I7 (accredited firm capacity below the reliability requirement) FAILs in FIVE — CAISO (2026-2029, up to 9,243 MW), MISO (2026 6,037 MW; 2027 3,659 MW), NEISO (2028 218 MW), PJM (2030 366 MW), NYISO (2026 36 MW; 2027 51 MW) — and I12 (reserve-margin band) FAILs in TWO, ERCOT (2027-2030, to -1.5%) and CAISO (2026-2029, to -3.1%). Union = 6 of 6. The magnitudes span four orders: NYISO's 36 MW is 0.11% of its requirement, CAISO's 2027 miss is 15.8% of its. ROOT CAUSE (unchanged, and still the live one): hydro is dispatched but excluded from the accredited firm-capacity ledger — accredited_firm_capacity_mw reads the persistent fleet, which never contains hydro. NEISO is NOT closed — I7 (2028) is its sole live T1-F blocker — and PJM, whose I4 leak this board called its only blocker, fails I7 too. In PJM, NEISO and NYISO it is now the ONLY thing between the ISO and a clean FC-1.
